issues.explanation: down() drops issue_date and then re-adds unique(queue_id, code); once the daily sequence has legitimately produced the same code on two dates (e.g. N001 yesterday and today) that ALTER fails, aborting the rollback after the column is already dropped, so the migration is not reliably reversible on a used database.

No test passes an explicit issue_date to the factory, so this branch (and its silent overwrite of the supplied issued_at date) is unexercised; add a case that sets issue_date explicitly and asserts both fields end up aligned.

The string-key fallback is unreachable (PHP already canonicalizes numeric string array keys to integers, and non-canonical keys are rejected at :106-109), so it adds dead code and a misleading comment.
The comment still says only code/status/issued_at are system-set, but issue_date is now also system-set and passed on line 63; update the comment so it matches the trusted-field list.

review.summary: The change implements priority-prefixed, per-day ticket codes as specified: default/custom prefixes with validation on Queue, a backfilled non-null issue_date with the new unique index, daily per-prefix allocation in IssueTicket and Ticket::nextCode, factory alignment, and updated docs plus extensive Pest coverage. The implementation is correct and well tested; the only substantive concern is that the tickets migration's down() can fail after daily codes repeat across days, with the remaining findings being nits.
